_comment: Mutation testing for survey templates (docs/architecture/survey-templates.md): the one check every template definition passes (languages, texts, answer types, rows, showWhen, what an answer becomes), the check on what a respondent filled in (shapes per answer type, branches, per-row answers, what a submit needs), turning a submitted survey into a transcript and claims (one line and one quote per answer, relation/status maps, the claim about a resource), the service (sending down a tree to each Accountable, who may open and answer, draft and submit), the seeding of the built-in templates, the survey-respondent sign-in check and the routes. WHY THESE FILES: every failure here is silent -- a showWhen read the wrong way asks a question nobody should get, an inverted relation map makes 'not me' an ownership claim, a recipient check too loose lets one person answer another's survey, a quote span off by one breaks the transcript view. Scoped like the sibling API configs: these files plus their own unit tests, which are self-contained (no repository paths outside the sandbox, no PostgreSQL). MUTATOR SET: StringLiteral and ObjectLiteral disabled, matching the sibling configs -- so the SQL in store.js is not mutated and stays the contract test's job (contract-tests/surveyTemplates.contract.test.js). Run: cd app/api && npm run test:mutation:surveys NOT YET MEASURED: this config ships with the feature; break is deliberately absent until a first run measures a score.
